newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa finance committee passes insurance bill.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa finance committee passes insurance bill.

text.p: South Africa's parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday unanimously passed the Insurance Amendment Bill -- another success for the Financial Services Board (FSB), trying to plug a loophole in existing legislation to protect consumers.
The bill covers the short-term insurance industry.

Presenting the bill to the committee, FSB head of research Franso van Zyl said the aim was to prevent brokers from collecting insurance premiums from clients unless authorised to do so by the insurers concerned.
"We have had numerous complaints about fraudulent activities such as not paying over premiums," he said.
As a result, clients had been left uncovered. The FSB had recently tried to intervene in two such cases but had lost them because it lacked the kind of powers that the bill would now provide.
The ultimate aim would be to make the registration of all brokers compulsory to "keep out the cowboys...and only get fit and proper people in."
This was currently being investigated by the FSB's policy board but was proving difficult to resolve because of the various vested interests involved.

The bill would also ban the use of sub-agents, which were difficult to monitor, and increase the guarantees that would have to be provided by brokers from 20 percent to 30 percent of premiums received a year.
Van Zyl said that the bill was part of an ongoing effort to revise regulations covering intermediaries such as brokers.
"This process has not been finalised but in the interim we are dealing with the most severe problems that we have," he said.

The bill follows hard on the heels of the Financial Institutions Amendment Bill, which was the first of about 20 bills planned by the FSB this year to improve investor protection and cater for the rapidly changing financial services market in South Africa.

The FSB regulates and supervises the financial services industry, excluding banks. This includes the short and long term insurance industry, unit trusts, participation bonds, pension funds, stock exchange and money market.

Other legislation being prepared by the FSB covers the advertising and canvassing of offshore business, controls over unit trusts and participation bonds, the protection of pension fund contributions and the regulation of the use of the title of stockbroker.
Van Zyl said that no matter how much legislation was improved, the board could not guarantee the absolute safety of the public's investments.
"We can try and assist in creating a safer environment...but you can never rule our fraudulent activities completely," Van Zyl said.
